chunks: And Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the one who is ascetic in this world:
He said: "The one who abandons what is lawful out of fear of its reckoning and abandons what is unlawful out of fear of its punishment."

key_terms.الزَّاهِد: The ascetic, one who practices zuhd

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true asceticism (zuhd) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes true asceticism (zuhd) from mere legalism by defining it as voluntarily abstaining from permissible pleasures out of fear of the final accounting, while avoiding the forbidden out of fear of punishment. This Hadith, recorded in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, highlights the Shia emphasis on *khawf* (awe/fear) as a driver for spiritual refinement beyond obligatory duties. It elevates piety from simple compliance to a state of spiritual vigilance regarding the subtle weight of permissible acts.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5861 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), peace be upon him, was asked about the one who is ascetic in this world.
Imam (as) said: "The one who abandons what is lawful out of fear of its reckoning and abandons what is unlawful out of fear of its punishment."
